title: Cap. IX Arg. 1 Resp.: head of error — reprobation is not the same as the decree of damning
pass_a_gloss: In the cause of predestination Jesuits and Arminians alike use a like argument, to which satisfaction was given by us before. In this argument the head of the error is, that reprobation or the decree of reprobating is presumed to be altogether the same as the decree of damning. But to us the decree of damning designates a peremptory sentence conceived from eternity in the mind of God the Judge, and confirmed by the good pleasure of the will, by which he established to punish with eternal death, on account of that sin, a man foresighted and considered as guilty of sin in the very exit of this life: but the decree of reprobating denotes the eternal good pleasure of God, not as Judge, but as freest Agent, by which he established with himself not to apply to certain persons that grace of special and unowed mercy which in fact would soften them, convert them, and lead them unto eternal life.
pass_b_english: Jesuits and Arminians use a like argument in the predestination debate — and we answered it before. The head of the error here is presuming reprobation, or the decree to reprobate, is altogether the same as the decree to damn. For us the decree to damn names a peremptory sentence conceived from eternity in the mind of God the Judge and confirmed by his will's good pleasure: to punish with eternal death, for that sin, a man foresighted and considered guilty of sin at this life's very exit. The decree to reprobate names God's eternal good pleasure not as Judge but as freest Agent: resolving not to apply to certain persons that grace of special unowed mercy which would in fact soften, convert, and lead them to eternal life.
source_text: In causa praedestinationis consimili argumento utuntur tum Jesuitae tum Arminiani, cui a nobis antea satisfactum fuit. In hoc argumento caput erroris est, quod reprobatio sive decretum reprobandi idem prorsus esse praesumitur, quod decretum damnandi. Nobis autem decretum damnandi designat sententiam peremptoriam in mente Dei Judicis ab aeterno conceptam, et voluntatis placito confirmatam, qua hominem praevisum et consideratum, ut peccati in ipso exitu hujus vitae reum, statuit propter illud peccatum aeterna morte punire: decretum autem reprobandi denotat aeternum placitum Dei, non ut Judicis, sed ut liberrimi Agentis, quo apud se statuit quibusdam personis non apponere illam specialis et indebitae misericordiae gratiam, quae de facto eos emolliret, converteret et ad vitam aeternam perduceret.
